[
1
]

Plaintiffs are seeking an authorization for
medical treatment against defendant D. B.

[
2
]

Defendant is a 30 year old man on welfare who is
currently living in an apartment with a roommate.

[
3
]

Dr Khalil Geagea and Ms Maxine Sigman, PhD,
psychologist, signed the following expert’s report dated June 15
th
,
2016
[1]
.

"˙ Mr.
B. is a 30 year old aboriginal man on welfare living with a roommate for 9
months at […] in [Town A]. He has refused permission for me to learn about his
previous history at Anna Laberge Hospital or to contact his mother with whom he
has not spoken in a year.

The emergency room staff did speak
with the mother who reported the patient has been abusing alcohol and drugs for
14 years and that he has frequent periods of homelessness. A cousin reported
Mr. B. has suffered a steep decline in functioning for 1 ‑2 years.
There is a report of him having put bleach in his grandmother’s food as he
thought she was poisoning him. The cousin also reported that the patient got
beat up in 2001 and sustained brain damage and needed hospitalization.

Mr. B. was admitted to the high
care unit of the Jewish General Hospital on June 7, 2016 in a psychotic state
feeling immensely paranoid. He was brought by police after an argument which a
roommate when he was wielding a knife as he believed the roommate stole his
welfare cheque. He gave 3 different accounts of this incident. He believes he
is a high ranking member of the Masonic order, a grand master which gives him
the right to bear arms. He reports he is also a member of the Illuminati.

On admission, he had very poor
insight and judgment. This has not changed. He is delusional, irritable, pacing
at times, screaming at nursing staff and refusing any psychiatric medication as
he feels convinced he is not mentally ill and does not need to be in hospital.
He has threatened a co-patient "I will take care
of your business" banging on his room door. He feels he is above the law
and reported that when he was last in court he was "suspended" and it
is the hospital staff whose "judgment is way off" .He feels he
is in a conspiracy in the hospital and that the staff is "paranoid and has
schizophrenic traits".

Without a previous history it is
difficult to know whether he suffers paranoid schizophrenia or substance abuse
disorder or both, concomitant with an anti-social personality.

We feel it is urgent that Mr. B. be
compelled by the law to take intra-muscular anti-psychotic medication as he
will not be able to be discharged from the high care unit or the hospital in
this serious psychotic state as he will be a danger to himself or others. His
condition worsened. He became very agitated on June 15, 2016 and required the
intervention of a Code White and an injection of Clopixol Accusphase 100 mg
stat. Since then, he remains easily irritable and very delusional.

We recommend further that a long-acting
injectable anti-psychotic medication ie. Sustenna 150 mg IM Q 4 weeks or
equivalent be ordered by the court for a period of 36 months due to the
patient’s dangerosity and acute psychotic state."

[
4
]

Plaintiffs filed two other medical reports
[2]
.

[
5
]

NOS.

[
6

In the second one, dated June 4
th
,

[
7

th
, 2016 Justice Magali

[3]

ANALYSIS
AND DECISION

Article
16,
C.C.Q
. :

16.

The authorization of the court is necessary
where the person who may give consent to care required by the state of health
of a minor or a person of full age who is incapable of giving his consent is
prevented from doing so or, without justification, refuses to do so; it is also
necessary where a person of full age who is incapable of giving his consent
categorically refuses to receive care, except in the case of hygienic care or
emergency (…).

[
8
]

On July 6
th
, 2015, Court of Appeal
established the conditions to give jurisdiction to the Superior Court to grant
a motion for authorization of medical treatment
[4]
.

«
Grille d’analyse

PREMIÈRE
ÉTAPE : LA COMPÉTENCE (art. 16 C.c.Q
.)?

Le juge ou le tribunal ne peut intervenir que s’il est
compétent à le faire.

Il doit
donc, dans une première étape, vérifier s’il est en présence des deux
conditions essentielles à l’existence de cette compétence : 1) inaptitude
à consentir et (2) refus catégorique. Si l’une ou l’autre de ces conditions
fait défaut, il n’a d’autre choix que de rejeter la demande.

Première
question (inaptitude)
: la personne majeure
est-elle inapte à consentir? Pour apprécier le tout, il y a lieu de se poser
les cinq sous-questions que voici :

o

Comprend-elle la nature de la maladie pour
laquelle un traitement lui est proposé?

o

Comprend-elle la nature et le but du traitement?

o

Saisit-elle les risques et les avantages du
traitement si elle le subit?

o

Comprend-elle les risques de ne pas subir le
traitement?

o

Sa capacité de comprendre est-elle affectée par
la maladie?

Deuxième
question (refus catégorique)
: la personne
majeure refuse-t-elle les soins pour lesquels l’ordonnance est recherchée?

➢

Ce n’est qu’en présence d’une preuve de refus
catégorique que le juge peut intervenir, le cas échéant.

➢

Si le traitement visé par l’ordonnance
recherchée n’a pas encore été offert, envisagé et discuté, il ne peut être
question de refus catégorique évidemment.

DEUXIÈME
ÉTAPE : EXERCICE DE LA COMPÉTENCE (art. 12
C.c.Q.
)

Ce n’est
que s’il conclut qu’il possède la compétence d’agir aux termes de l’
article 16

C.c.Q.

que le juge ou le tribunal peut passer à cette seconde étape.

THE
INCAPACITY

o

COMPREND-IL
LA NATURE DE LA MALADIE POUR LAQUELLE UN TRAITEMENT LUI AIT PROPOSÉ?

[
9
]

I am convinced that the defendant does not understand
his illness because he is convinced that his only illness is high blood
pressure problem.

o

COMPREND-IIL LA NATURE ET LE BUT DU TRAITEMENT?

[
10
]

First, I don’t have the answer in the report.
Secondly, Dr Gaegea was not present to answer that question.

o

SAISIT-IL LES RISQUES ET LES AVANTAGES DU TRAITEMENT S’IL LE SUBIT ?

[
11
]

This question is not answered.

[
12
]

Ms Maxine Sigman PhD testified but could not
answer about this risks and advantages of the proposed treatment.

o

COMPREND-IL LES RISQUES DE NE PAS SUBIR LE TRAITEMENT?

[
13
]

This question is not answered.

o

SA CAPACITÉ DE COMPRENDRE EST-ELLE AFFECTÉE PAR LA MALADIE ?

[
14
]

This question is not answered.

THE
CATEGORICAL REFUSAL

[
15
]

Defendant’s capacity to understand is impaired
by his illness.

[
16
]

The Court must be convinced of a categorical
refusal.

[
17
]

Defendant accepted to take oral medication "because he was blackmailed", following the Lewis judgment.

[
18
]

I cannot conclude that we are in presence of a
categorical refusal.

[
19
]

FOR THESE REASONS THE COURT :

[
20
]

DISMISSES
the
application for authorization of medical treatment.
